cross_field_papers.title: Regime-switching models for electricity spot prices: Introducing heteroskedastic base regime dynamics and shifted spike distributions
cross_field_papers.abstract: We calibrate Markov regime-switching (MRS) models to mean daily spot prices from the EEX market. Our empirical study shows that (i) models with shifted spike regime distributions lead to more realistic models of electricity spot prices and that (ii) introducing heteroskedasticity in the base regime leads to better spike identification and goodness-of-fit than in MRS models with the standard mean-reverting, constant volatility dynamics.regime-switching, heteroskedasticity, electricity spot price

cross_field_papers.title: Goodness-of-fit testing for regime-switching models
cross_field_papers.abstract: In this paper we propose a novel goodness-of-fit testing scheme for regime-switching models. We consider models with an observable, as well as, a latent state process. The test is based on the Kolmogorov-Smirnov supremum-distance statistic and the concept of the weighted empirical distribution function. We apply the proposed scheme to test whether a 2-state Markov regime-switching model fits electricity spot price data.Regime-switching; Goodness-of-fit; Weighted empirical distribution function; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

cross_field_papers.title: Regime switching GARCH models
cross_field_papers.abstract: We develop univariate regime-switching GARCH (RS-GARCH) models wherein the conditional variance switches in time from one GARCH process to another. The switching is governed by a time-varying probability, specified as a function of past information. We provide sufficient conditions for stationarity and existence of moments. Because of path dependence, maximum likehood estimation is infeasible. By enlarging the parameter space to include the state variables, Bayesian estimation using a Gibbs sampling algorithm is feasible. We apply this model using the NASDAQ daily returns series.GARCH; regime switching; Bayesian inference

cross_field_papers.title: Estimation of Markov regime-switching regression models with endogenous switching
cross_field_papers.abstract: Following Hamilton (1989), estimation of Markov regime-switching regressions nearly always relies on the assumption that the latent state variable controlling the regime change is exogenous. We incorporate endogenous switching into a Markov-switching regression and develop strategies for identification and estimation. Identification requires instruments, which can be found in observed exogenous variables that influence the transition probabilities of the regime-switching process, as in the so-called time-varying transition probability case. However, even with fixed transition probabilities, the lagged state variable can serve as an instrument provided it is exogenous and the state process is serially dependent. This is true even though the lagged state is unobserved. A straightforward test for endogeneity is also presented. Monte Carlo experiments confirm that the estimation procedures perform quite well in practice. We apply the endogenous switching model to the volatility feedback model of equity returns given in Turner, Startz and Nelson (1989).Econometric models

cross_field_papers.title: Modeling electricity spot prices: Regime switching models with price-capped spike distributions
cross_field_papers.abstract: We calibrate Markov regime-switching (MRS) models to spot (log-)prices from two major power markets. We show that while the price-capped (or truncated) spike distributions do not give any advantage over the standard specification in case of moderately spiky markets (such as NEPOOL), they improve the fit and yield significantly different results in case of extremely spiky markets (such as the Australian NSW market).Electricity spot price; Markov regime-switching model; Price spike; Price cap; Truncated distribution

bridge_insights.insight: Unsupervised anomaly detection models designed for industrial time series with regime drifts can inform market regime detection by adapting their state-conditioned association learning to identify structural changes in financial time series that correspond to distinct market regimes.
bridge_insights.connection_to_core_problem: The core problem involves identifying market regimes using unsupervised clustering of price and volume features; the state-conditioned association learning approach from industrial anomaly detection can help distinguish true regime shifts from noise or normal variation in financial data.

bridge_insights.insight: Fully unsupervised anomaly detection frameworks that handle contaminated data can be adapted to detect outliers in financial market data, which may indicate regime shifts, allowing for more robust identification of market states without requiring clean training data.
bridge_insights.connection_to_core_problem: Market regime detection often relies on identifying deviations from typical behavior; the contamination-aware models from anomaly detection literature can help filter out false positives and improve the reliability of regime identification in noisy financial datasets.

bridge_insights.insight: Geometric observables derived from spectral embeddings can serve as regime-shift detectors in financial markets, offering a way to identify transitions between different market states that may enhance momentum strategy performance by aligning trades with regime characteristics.
bridge_insights.connection_to_core_problem: The core problem involves improving momentum strategies through regime identification; geometric observables provide a mathematical framework for detecting regime changes that could be used to adjust momentum signals accordingly.

bridge_insights.insight: Hierarchical clustering algorithms used for event detection in textual data can be adapted to cluster financial time series based on news sentiment or other textual features, potentially improving the accuracy of regime classification by incorporating external information sources.
bridge_insights.connection_to_core_problem: Market regimes may be influenced by events captured in news or social media; hierarchical clustering methods from NLP can be applied to integrate such information into unsupervised regime detection models.

bridge_insights.insight: Network-based clustering algorithms developed for anomaly detection in cybersecurity can be repurposed to identify clusters of stocks or market segments that behave similarly under different regimes, enhancing the ability to group assets according to their response to regime changes.
bridge_insights.connection_to_core_problem: Identifying coherent groups of assets that respond similarly to market regimes is crucial for momentum strategies; network clustering techniques offer a way to discover such groups without prior labeling.
